newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: ATHLETICS-BEVILACQUA AND CAPOBIANCO TO LEARN FATE.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BEVILACQUA AND CAPOBIANCO TO LEARN FATE.

text.p: Italian high jumper Antonella Bevilacqua and Australian sprinter Dean Capobianco will learn within the space of a month whether they are to be banned from competition after positive drugs tests this year.
International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF) general secretary Istvan Gyulai said on Wednesday dates had been set for an independent arbitration panel to meet.
"The panel will meet to discuss the Bevilacqua case on Saturday, October 26," he said. "The panel will consider the Capobianco case on Sunday, November 24,"
Both cases will be heard in the federation's headquarters in Monte Carlo.
The pair were allowed to compete at the Atlanta Olympics despite failing drugs tests after the IAAF's legal advisors said the federation could be sued successfully in a civil court.
Bevilacqua tested positive twice last May for the stimulant ephedrine but an Italian panel ruled she had taken the drug by accident and did not impose the statutory three-month ban.
Capobianco tested positive for the steroid stanozolol, the drug used by Ben Johnson at the 1988 Seoul Olympics, at a meeting in the Dutch town of Hengelo in the same month.
He escaped a four-year ban when his national governing body Athletics Australia cleared him on the grounds that the testing procedures had been seriously flawed.

In Atlanta Gyulai said the IAAF's decision to let the pair compete had been "embarrassing" and senior federation officials made it clear they regarded both athletes as being guilty of doping offences.
But the IAAF council decided it would not use its power to overturn the decision of a national federation and instead refer the matter to arbitration.

Three years ago the council banned Germany's former double world sprint champion Katrin Krabbe for two years for unsportsmanlike conduct after she admitted taking drugs only to see the decision overturned in a civil court.

The IAAF's grand prix commission met here on Wednesday to decide next year's calendar in what will be another packed year for the sport with the world indoor championships in Paris followed by the outdoor championships in Athens.
The calendar will be announced by IAAF president Primo Nebiolo on Thursday.
